endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is not realized if a dashboard exists but omits methodology or contested segments.
endpoint_ledger.description: The dispute reaches a terminal state where both city and contractor-facing observers can evaluate permit wait performance using a common, published methodology.
endpoint_ledger.label: Shared auditable metrics established

meta.important_question: Will the city and contractors converge on a shared, auditable definition of permit wait time that explains the 40% reduction claim versus the 10-to-18-day median increase claim?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The scenario explicitly prioritizes numerical consistency and uncertainty around metrics.
realization_criteria: A public or formally shared methodology defines permit classes, start and end timestamps, and summary statistics used.
Both the city's reduction claim and the contractors' increase claim are either reconciled or explicitly segmented into non-contradictory populations.
Subsequent public statements cite the same metric framework rather than incompatible figures.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Central scenario tension is unresolved measurement conflict with explicit uncertainty to preserve.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: A dashboard that only reports aggregate citywide averages without addressing the contested median claim may not satisfy realization.
endpoint_ledger.description: A public dashboard becomes the operative accountability endpoint only if it provides meaningful transparency rather than symbolic publication.
endpoint_ledger.label: Substantive public dashboard launched

meta.important_question: Will the mayor's public dashboard materially disclose contested wait-time methodology and segment-level outcomes, rather than serving as a messaging device?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: The dashboard is a key mechanism and possible endpoint if it becomes the durable transparency structure.
realization_criteria: It includes permit wait measures with clear definitions and update cadence.
It discloses enough segmentation to test the contested claims relevant to small contractors.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Mayor desire is explicit, but substance and launch remain uncertain at T0.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: Public statements about 'considering options' do not realize this endpoint absent a formal filing.
endpoint_ledger.description: Contractors escalate from threat to filed legal action challenging the permit system, metrics, or administrative treatment.
endpoint_ledger.label: Formal contractor litigation

meta.important_question: Will small contractors convert the lawsuit threat into formal legal action?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Legal escalation is one of the clearest terminal alternatives implied by the scenario.
realization_criteria: A complaint, petition, or equivalent formal legal filing is submitted by or on behalf of small contractors.
City attorney or court process is formally engaged.
Public dispute shifts from threat posture to active legal case management.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: Threat is explicit but not yet realized.

endpoint_ledger.contradiction_notes: This endpoint is not realized by isolated anecdotes alone unless they become the accepted basis for broad assessment.
endpoint_ledger.description: A terminal assessment emerges on whether the new permit system improved, worsened, or unevenly redistributed wait outcomes.
endpoint_ledger.label: New system net assessment

meta.important_question: At the end of the observed horizon, is the new permit system shown to improve, worsen, or unevenly redistribute wait times across applicant groups?

endpoint_ledger.rationale: Later simulation evidence should be able to compare terminal outcome claims rather than only replay process moves.
realization_criteria: Credible evidence demonstrates one of three observable outcomes: citywide improvement, net worsening, or segmented redistribution across applicant types.
Key public actors stop contesting the existence of any measurable outcome direction, even if they dispute blame.
Decision-making and public messaging begin to operate from that accepted outcome direction.
endpoint_ledger.status_basis: The scenario implies a final question about actual system performance beyond process arguments.

risk_flags.description: City and contractor figures may use incompatible statistics, populations, or time windows.
A 40% reduction claim may be true for aggregate or selected categories while small contractors experience worse median outcomes.
Dashboard initiative may function as reputational signaling without resolving methodological dispute.
Formal legal action could harden positions and reduce flexibility for collaborative metric repair.
Concerned staff may withhold doubts due to organizational pressure, delaying correction of flawed claims.

primary_tensions: small business trust in city operations
simulation_brief.summary: A municipal government claims a new permit system reduced wait times by 40%, while small contractors assert median wait times increased from 10 to 18 days. The mayor seeks a public dashboard, permitting staff attribute delays to incomplete applications, and contractors are threatening litigation. Numerical claims are contested and may rely on different metrics or populations.
simulation_brief.time_zero_posture: early dispute with unresolved measurement conflict and moderate escalation risk
uncertainty_notes: The city and contractors may be measuring different permit classes, time windows, or summary statistics.
No verified source dataset is provided at initialization.
Lawsuit threat is present but not yet realized.
Extent of public awareness beyond direct stakeholders is unclear.
